ety.text: Literally, “steam-horse”. Similar to English horsepower, the word derives from the initial use to rate steam engines by comparison with the power which a draught horse could sustain over several hours. Later, use expanded to cover steam turbines, and then all other sources of sustained power, measured in several ways, including measurements for taxation purposes (tax horsepower) which bear little resemblance to mechanical horsepower. In most or all English-speaking countries, this usage has lapsed, but in France it persists.
